title: Mould observation diary
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Living things and their habitats (Frozen Kingdom)
source: Seeded from science/y6 lesson 12 (Mould observation diary (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 12: Micro-organisms: helpful and harmful. To understand that micro-organisms are tiny living things that can be helpful or harmful

questions.q: Give one helpful micro-organism and what it does.
questions.a: For example: yeast makes bread rise.
questions.model: Name it: yeast. Say the job: makes bread rise. Say how: it gives off gas bubbles. So: yeast is helpful because it makes bread rise.

questions.q: Why do we wash our hands before eating?
questions.a: To remove harmful bacteria and viruses.

questions.q: Why must the mould bag stay sealed?
questions.a: Mould spores can make people ill if breathed in.

questions.q: Core: Set up the mould bag with an adult (a slice of bread, a few drops of water, sealed bag). Draw it on day 1 and plan when to observe it again.
questions.a: Day 1 drawing; observe on days 3, 5 and 7 through the bag.
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: dampen the bread with three drops of water, seal, label with the date, put in a warm place.

questions.q: Extend: Predict: will mould grow faster in a warm or a cold place? Why?
questions.a: Warm: micro-organisms grow faster in warmth.

questions.q: Stretch: Why do we keep food in the fridge?
questions.a: The cold slows the growth of bacteria and moulds.

questions.q: Big question: are all germs bad?
questions.a: No: many micro-organisms are helpful, such as yeast and yoghurt bacteria.
